name: nest#20481 compose web-api env vars centrally
description:
# chore(rust-backend): compose web-api environment variables centrally

Every environment variable that changes web-api's behaviour was read
where it was used: `PERIPHERAL_CACHE_CAPACITY_BYTES` in
`graphql_schema`, `FACTBIRD_LIVE_DATA_CACHE` /
`FACTBIRD_CACHE_REQUEST_COALESCING` / `FACTBIRD_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`
inside the moka cache constructor, `IAM_ENTRY_ARN` inside a per-request
resolver, and OAuth/MCP/IoT settings inside their own `from_env()`
helpers. No naming convention spans these, so there was no single place
to see what web-api is configurable with, and several settings
travelled as `Option` only because the default lived at the read site.

Now, compose `web_api::config::WebApiConfig` once in `main` and hand
it down. `fb_datafusion_cache::TimeseriesCacheConfig` does the same for
the cache tunables the cache used to read from the process environment
itself. Environment reads now happen only in
`rust-backend/web-api/src/config.rs` and
`libraries/rust/fb-datafusion-cache/src/caching/config.rs`, through
shared helpers in a new `fb_rust::env` module (`env_or`,
`parse_env_flag`, behind an `env` feature).

```diff
 async_main
+  config = WebApiConfig::from_env()
-  server(url, aws_config)
+  server(url, aws_config, config)
-    cross_account::from_env(..)                # read IoT env itself
+    cross_account::client_provider(.., &config.devices.cross_account_iot)
     server_with_deps(ServerDeps { config, .. })
-      graphql_schema(..)
-        env PERIPHERAL_CACHE_CAPACITY_BYTES, CLOUD_SUBDOMAIN
-        QueryDatafusionTables::new(.., capacity)
-          TimeseriesTableCacheMoka::new          # read FACTBIRD_* itself
+      graphql_schema(.., &config)
+        QueryDatafusionTables::new(.., config.timeseries_cache)
+        schema.data(config)                    # resolvers: ctx.data::<WebApiConfig>()
```

Each variable keeps its parse rule (`USE_LOCAL_GATEWAY` stays
presence-based, `IGNORE_MISSING_MIGRATIONS` still compares to `"true"`,
the `FACTBIRD_*` flags still accept `1`/`true`) and its default, with
two exceptions at the explicitly-empty/zero boundary. Neither is
reachable in a deployed environment:

- `PERIPHERAL_CACHE_CAPACITY_BYTES=0` used to parse to `Some(0)` and
  take the cached branch (a moka cache with `max_capacity(0)`). Now
  `enabled()` is `capacity_bytes > 0`, so an explicit `0` takes the
  uncached branch, a different physical plan. This applies to the
  napi bindings too.
- `DB_HOST_READ_ONLY=""` used to satisfy `if let Ok(..)` and take the
  read-only branch with an empty endpoint. Now `is_empty()` routes it
  back to the primary pool. The CDK always sets it to
  `dbCluster.clusterReadEndpoint.hostname`, never empty.

Both `from_env` constructors `warn!` on values that fail to parse and
fall back to the default, so `FACTBIRD_*` typos are no longer silent.
The warning lives in `fb_rust::env::env_or`, so `fb-datafusion-cache`
gets `tracing` through `fb-rust` rather than depending on it directly.

Out of scope: a naming convention for feature flags, and a system that
changes settings without a service restart.

- Every field resolves to a concrete value, with defaults in `Default`
  impls next to the field. Where absence is the setting, an
  `enabled()` predicate over empty/zero replaces the `Option`:
  `TimeseriesCacheConfig::enabled()` (capacity `0`),
  `CertificateArchiveConfig::enabled()`,
  `CrossAccountIotConfig::enabled()`.
- `IAM_ENTRY_ARN`, which deployed environments always set but local
  runs may not, is stored as the raw `Result` of the environment read.
  Consumers `expect` it with their prior messages the moment they
  reach the IAM dependency, so a local process still boots and fails
  only there, as it did with `std::env::var(..).expect(..)`.
- The `config` module doc tables every variable, the field it lands
  in, and its default, plus the variables shared libraries
  (`fb_postgres_utils`, `fb_influxdb_utils`, `fb_permission_checker`,
  `fb_aws_config`, ...) parse on web-api's behalf. Those stay where
  they are, since `ingester`, `background-processor` and the napi
  bindings share them.
- `TimeseriesTableCacheMoka::new` and the
  `dynamodb_peripheral_data_*_with_cache` builders take
  `TimeseriesCacheConfig` instead of a bare capacity, so tests and
  benchmarks build an explicit config instead of reading `FACTBIRD_*`
  from the process environment. Their effective settings are
  unchanged, since `Default` matches what the unset environment
  produced. `dynamodb_peripheral_data_seconds_30_with_live_cache` is
  dropped; the plain `_with_cache` builder covers it now that the
  config carries the live-tail TTL.
- `fb-datafusion-dynamodb-tables` re-exports `TimeseriesCacheConfig`,
  so web-api and the napi bindings need no direct dependency on
  `fb-datafusion-cache`.

Closes https://github.com/FactbirdHQ/nest/issues/22189

name: nest#22230 fixed app-token step ids
description:
# chore(infrastructure/ci-cd): stop renumbering app token step ids

Each job's token step took its id from a module-level counter (`gt0`,
`gt1`, ...), so adding or removing one job renumbered the ids in every
workflow.

Now, give the token step the fixed id `github-token`, and move it into
the composite action `.github/actions/generate-github-token` so the
token steps are no longer duplicated in every job.

A local action is read from the workspace, so the checkout now runs
first, with `github.token` and `persist-credentials: false`. A persisted
credential would take precedence over the app token, which git
operations such as the push in `update-github-runner` rely on.

`ci-ui-dashboard` no longer mints a second token before `Deploy to
Next`. Nothing read it, and the job's first token is seconds old when
the deploy runs, since master skips `Build`.

Mind that `action.yml` is committed by hand until
https://github.com/FactbirdHQ/nest/pull/18579 generates it.

Closes https://github.com/FactbirdHQ/nest/issues/22229

name: nixfiles#60 comment-audit
description:
# feat(claude): audit added code comments with Jev

Agent sessions write comments that restate the code, narrate the change
that wrote them, or repeat a fact stated elsewhere. The code-comments rule
forbids most of it, but nothing measured a diff against the rule.

Now, add a `comment-audit` skill whose scorer asks Jev six narrow questions
about every comment block a diff adds, and turns the answers into one
action per comment: remove, into-code, move-to-commit, dedupe, trim or
keep. The session reading the code makes the edit or files the finding.

- `rules/writing.md` puts names before comments, with units last and steps
  extracted into functions, and runs the skill before a commit that adds
  comments.
- `review-code-comments` scores the PR first and treats the flags as where
  to start. Its necessity test also covers shorthand names that want
  spelling out, history, and a fact repeated across sites.

Each question names one failure mode, because a single quality Score mixes
dimensions and rates a long "why" comment as highly as a useful one. A text
match on issue numbers, finding ids and past-tense words backs up the
history question, which scored a bare `#21471` near 0.6.

Mind that the scorer sends one Jev request per added comment block and
needs `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. Without the key the skill applies its table by
hand and says the scorer did not run.

Closes https://github.com/martinjlowm/nixfiles/issues/59

name: agents-mj#109 bump claude-config
description:
# chore(claude-agents): verify review claims before acting on them

Fleet sessions that address review threads implemented a reviewer's
statement of fact without checking it. On
https://github.com/FactbirdHQ/nest/pull/22340 one session rewrote a fetch
for an Apollo Client race fixed versions before the one ui-app pins, and a
later session reverted it.

Now, take nixfiles b51a17d, whose `pr-comments` skill hands such a claim
to `review-claim-verifier` before agreeing. The image already ships the
verifier. The bump also brings `pr-description`'s rule that issue bodies
stay unwrapped; the other commits in the range touch only the laptop.

Mind that the change reaches sessions only once the agent image is
rebuilt and pushed, because skills are baked into it.

Refs https://github.com/martinjlowm/nixfiles/issues/54

name: synthetic: fix plus unrelated refactor plus a dependency bump
description:
# fix(web-api): reject empty device ids

Empty device ids crashed the sync job.

Now, reject them at the resolver. While here, rename `DeviceRepo` to `DeviceStore` across the crate, move the retry helper into `fb-rust`, and bump `aws-sdk-iot` to 1.60 for the new paginator.
